I stepped on a pretty scary, top-class bug while porting from MT4 to MT5 😱

■ Symptom
A settlement-error dialog kept appearing repeatedly. When I checked the position, neither SL nor TP was set, and 5 days had passed 😱 I had no choice but to close it manually.

■ Cause
MT4's OrderTicket() is an int (32-bit).
MT5's PositionGetTicket() is a ulong (64-bit).

The ticket number exceeded the int limit (about 2.1 billion), and the cast dropped the upper bits, turning it into a different number.

It did not reproduce in the tester, and it did not occur with other brokers.
Apparently, at Vantage the ticket numbers exceed 2.1 billion.

If you have an EA ported from MT4, please check whether it still uses an int ticket ⚠️

I was really lucky to find such a serious, fatal bug 😌

What matters in overseas FX isn't just whether you can earn, but whether you can properly withdraw what you earned.

After actually withdrawing 30 million yen, I felt XS's bank withdrawals are quite excellent 🐷🔥

[Overseas FX: a bit scary if you don't know this]
There was an unexpected difference between Exness and XS in bank withdrawals

I've made many large withdrawals from both, but there was a difference in how funds arrive, so let me tell you.

✅ In Exness's case

The requested withdrawal amount and the amount arriving at the bank always match.

For example, if you withdraw 1 million yen x 5 requests, the bank also receives 1 million yen x 5 arrivals.

For risk management, I'm mindful of:
・under 1 million yen per request
・under 10 million yen total per day

✅ In XS's case

Multiple withdrawals can arrive bundled together.

For example, even if you request 1 million yen x 6 withdrawals, the bank may receive a single arrival of 6 million yen.

At first I was also mindful of:
・under 1 million yen per request
・under 10 million yen total per day

but suddenly 5 million yen hit my bank in one go and I panicked so much my whole body fat trembled.

However, in the end there was no problem on the bank's side either, so now I'm only mindful of keeping the daily total under 10 million yen.

By the way, here's why I split up large withdrawals ↓

I personally haven't had any inquiries from my bank over withdrawals from Exness or XS.

That said, I have experienced bank inquiries and account freezes several times.

① Fintokei: a few confirmation phone calls from the bank
I think funds arrived from overseas around the Czech Republic, and I got a few calls asking "This isn't money used for things like war, is it?"

② PayPay Bank: instant freeze with no questions asked
It's unclear whether overseas FX withdrawals were the cause, but with no inquiry from the bank, the account was frozen. I was able to withdraw, though.

③ Mizuho Bank / SBI Bank: account freeze & withdrawals not possible
I got caught up in a P2P scam and the accounts were frozen. I couldn't even withdraw. This has nothing to do with overseas FX, though.

That's all the bank trouble I've experienced.

In other words, even though I keep repeating such large bank withdrawals, the only case where overseas FX withdrawals may have affected a bank account is the single PayPay Bank freeze.

And that was before the June 2026 amendment of the Payment Services Act.

At least in my experience, there has not been a single trouble I could confirm was affected by the legal amendment.

That doesn't mean it will stay safe from now on, so I take care to spread out large withdrawals and leave as little money as possible in the receiving bank account ↓
